claims.claim: two African calanoids: population-increase threshold 46 and 79 µg C/L, on Cryptomonas at 17 °C
claims.location: p. 656 (PDF p. 9), Table 5 (read on the page image); abstract p. 648 (PDF p. 1)
claims.quote: Threshold for population increase … M. meridianus 78.5 … T. spectabilis 45.8
claims.conditions: laboratory, 17 °C, seven Cryptomonas levels 0.05–2.5 mg C/L; Tropodiaptomus spectabilis 45.8 ± 135.1 and Metadiaptomus meridianus 78.5 ± 149.1 µg C/L (x̄ ± 95 % C.L.), the food level at which the regression of eggs ind.⁻¹ d⁻¹ (Rpi) on food reaches zero; animals from two South African reservoirs (Midmar, Albert Falls)
claims.note: now read in full, so '(abstract only)' can go. The 95 % confidence limits are far wider than the values themselves, and the author says the two species' thresholds 'did not differ'; the table could add '(95 % CL ±135–149)'. Breeding thresholds were 17.7 and 59.7, development thresholds 10.9 and 4.9 µg C/L

claims.claim: calanoid thresholds are ~1.0–1.5× Daphnia's (Hart 1996; Kreutzer & Lampert 1999), not lower
claims.conditions: Hart: 17 °C on Cryptomonas; the Daphnia values it is set against (40, 54 and 58 µg C/L in the paper's Table 3.3-3, Kreutzer & Lampert 1999) are at 20 °C on Scenedesmus and were not checked here
claims.note: Hart's inputs check (45.8, 78.5). Working: calanoid 46–79 vs Daphnia 40–58 gives pairwise ratios 46/58 = 0.79 to 79/40 = 1.98; means 62.2/50.7 = 1.23. So '~1.0–1.5×' is a fair central summary but the span is 0.8–2.0×, across different foods and temperatures, and Hart's 95 % limits (±135–149 µg C/L) cannot rule out a lower calanoid threshold: 'not lower' is a modelling choice the data allow, not a finding. Hart 1996 itself makes no comparison with Daphnia

notes: Other values: maximal survival ~40 % in M. meridianus (high naupliar mortality, mostly fungal parasitism) vs ~90 % in T. spectabilis; survival asymptotes at 0.35–0.5 mg C/L; clutches 5-fold larger in M. meridianus; interspecific equivalence (breakpoint) food levels 82 µg C/L for egg production and 165 for population increase, T. spectabilis superior below them; development responses of M. meridianus saturate at ~0.35 mg C/L. The species are tropical/subtropical diaptomids, not the Leptodiaptomus of Maine lakes.
